name: Catching when models hallucinate or go wrong
gist: Models sometimes confidently say false things. These papers detect when a model is uncertain, lying, or relying on spurious patterns rather than true reasoning.
explain: Language models sometimes generate text that is false, nonsensical, or based on patterns that don't generalize. When asked 'What is 2 plus 2?', a model might answer '5' with high confidence. This is called hallucination. The model isn't reasoning; it's matching patterns in its training data. These papers try to detect when a model is uncertain, contradicting itself, or leaning on spurious correlations — surface-level patterns that happen to be true in the training set but don't reflect real reasoning.

Detection methods look for red flags inside the model. High uncertainty in the internal states might signal doubt. Incoherence — when different parts of the model disagree — might mean the model is guessing. Some papers check whether the model's explanation of a prediction actually holds up under scrutiny: if you ask the model to justify its answer and the justification doesn't logically follow, it's probably hallucinating. Others measure whether the model is truly using the features it claims to use or just pattern-matching shallow correlations. The aim is to catch failures before they reach the user, so the system can fall back to a human, ask for clarification, or refuse to answer.

papers.title: From Flat Facts to Sharp Hallucinations: Detecting Stubborn Errors via Gradient Sensitivity
papers.contribution: Detects high-confidence factual errors by distinguishing stable knowledge (flat minima) from brittle memorization (sharp minima).

papers.title: Gradients with Respect to Semantics Preserving Embeddings Tell the Uncertainty of Large Language Model
papers.contribution: Provides efficient and effective uncertainty estimates for free-form generation, achieving superior performance than state-of-the-art methods particularly for multiple valid responses.

papers.title: Grounding or Guessing? Visual Signals for Detecting Hallucinations in Sign Language Translation
papers.contribution: The proposed measure predicts hallucination rates across benchmarks and architectures, distinguishes grounded from guessed tokens, and enables risk estimation without references.

papers.title: LatentQA: Teaching LLMs to Decode Activations Into Natural Language
papers.contribution: Outperforms competitive baselines on supervised reading tasks including hidden system prompt uncovery and relational knowledge extraction, while demonstrating steerability and good scaling.

papers.title: Optimal Transport Group Counterfactual Explanations
papers.contribution: Enable generalization with fewer parameters, preserve group geometry, and provide mathematical characterization of group counterfactuals for linear classifiers.

papers.title: Semantic Uncertainty Quantification of Hallucinations in LLMs: A Quantum Tensor Network Based Method
papers.contribution: Detects hallucinations robustly across different generation lengths and quantization levels, showing consistent AUROC and AURAC improvements over baselines.

papers.title: Synthesising Counterfactual Explanations via Label-Conditional Gaussian Mixture Variational Autoencoders
papers.contribution: The method ensures robustness to input changes as paths converge to fixed centroids, provides diverse recourse options, and supports user-specified actionability constraints via gradient optimization.

papers.title: Thought Branches: Interpreting LLM Reasoning Requires Resampling
papers.contribution: Reveals that normative self-preservation sentences have small non-resilient effects on decisions, while on-policy sentence insertions produce larger and more consistent effects than off-policy edits.

papers.title: ATEX-CF: Attack-Informed Counterfactual Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
papers.contribution: ATEX-CF generates faithful, concise, and plausible explanations on synthetic and real-world node classification benchmarks, demonstrating the value of integrating adversarial insights into counterfactual reasoning.

papers.title: Attention Sinks as Internal Signals for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Produces state-of-the-art hallucination detection across popular datasets and LLMs while explaining previous methods' implicit dependence on attention sinks.

papers.title: Automatic Layer Selection for Hallucination Detection
papers.contribution: FEPoID consistently identifies optimal or near-optimal layers for hallucination detection across question answering and summarization benchmarks with negligible computational overhead.

papers.title: Counterfactual Explanations on Robust Perceptual Geodesics
papers.contribution: Outperforms baselines on three vision datasets and reveals failure modes hidden under standard metrics.

papers.title: DOUBT: Decoupled Object-level Understanding and Bridging via vMF-based Trustworthiness for Hallucination Detection in MLLMs
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on multiple benchmarks, demonstrating robustness and generalizability for MLLM hallucination detection.

papers.title: Density-Guided Robust Counterfactual Explanations on Tabular Data under Model Multiplicity
papers.contribution: The method achieves superior validity under model multiplicity while significantly reducing query costs compared to ensemble-based baselines.

papers.title: Diagnosing Failures in Generalization from Task-Relevant Representational Geometry
papers.contribution: Shows that geometric properties of in-distribution manifolds (effective dimensionality and utility) consistently predict weaker OOD performance more reliably than in-distribution accuracy.

papers.title: Evaluating and Steering Modality Preferences in Multi-modal LLMs
papers.contribution: Reveals all 20 tested MLLMs demonstrate clear modality preferences statistically associated with downstream task performance; method effectively amplifies preference toward desired direction improving multi-modal tasks.

papers.title: Fresh in memory: Training-order recency is linearly encoded in language model activations
papers.contribution: Shows activations linearly encode training order with ~90% accuracy for early/late distinction and ~80% accuracy for exact training stage prediction.

papers.title: GAUSS: Graph-Assisted Uncertainty Quantification using Structure and Semantics for Long-Form Generation in LLMs
papers.contribution: Offers more interpretable and theoretically grounded uncertainty measures than coarse, sentence-level scores by capturing semantic content and structural coherence.

papers.title: Hallucination Detection from Structural Reasoning Model
papers.contribution: Most advantageous on longer, dependency-rich traces like math and code generation, providing structured perspective on chain-of-thought evaluation.

papers.title: Hessian-Enhanced Token Attribution (HETA): Interpreting Autoregressive LLMs
papers.contribution: HETA establishes a new standard for interpretability in autoregressive language models, outperforming existing methods in attribution faithfulness and alignment with human annotations.

papers.title: Information Flow Reveals When to Trust Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieve average AUROC of 0.709, exceeding runner-up 0.676, for uncertainty estimation in RAG while maintaining moderate computational cost via layer-wise information flow analysis.

papers.title: Instruction Lens Score: Your Instruction Contributes a Powerful Object Hallucination Detector for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: InsLen serves as a plug-and-play hallucination detector without auxiliary models or training, consistently outperforming existing methods across benchmarks and MLLM architectures.

papers.title: Interpreting and Enhancing Emotional Circuits in Large Vision-Language Models via Cross-Modal Information Flow
papers.contribution: The discovered emotional circuits enable regulated information routing to strengthen attention flow and amplify semantic activation, significantly improving performance on comprehensive MER-UniBench and mitigating emotional hallucinations.

papers.title: Latent Planning Emerges with Scale
papers.contribution: Latent planning increases with scale; models identify rhymes ahead of time; even smaller models have nascent planning mechanisms.

papers.title: One Probe Won’t Catch Them All: Towards Targeted Deception Detection
papers.contribution: Organizations should define specific threat models and deploy appropriately matched probes rather than seeking a universal deception detector, with oracle analysis showing 0.108 AUC potential versus 0.032 for universal probes.

papers.title: Outcome Rewards Do Not Guarantee Verifiable or Causally Important Reasoning
papers.contribution: Shows RLVR improves accuracy without reliably improving reasoning quality, but joint rewards match accuracy while improving causally important and sufficient reasoning.

papers.title: ProbeLLM: Automating Principled Diagnosis of LLM Failures
papers.contribution: ProbeLLM reveals broader, cleaner, finer-grained failure landscapes than static benchmarks, enabling shift from case-centric toward structured weakness discovery.

papers.title: Spilled Energy in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Training-free metrics demonstrate robust hallucination detection across nine benchmarks and state-of-the-art LLMs without introducing overhead, with competitive cross-task generalization.

papers.title: The Geometry of Reasoning: Self-Evaluation via Layerwise Trajectory Evolution
papers.contribution: Consistently outperform state-of-the-art baselines in AUROC, AUPR, and FPR@95 across eight LRMs and seven benchmarks.

papers.title: The Information Geometry of Softmax: Probing and Steering
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that dual steering enhances controllability and stability of concept manipulation beyond existing steering methods.

papers.title: VeriTrail: Closed-Domain Hallucination Detection with Traceability
papers.contribution: Outperforms baseline methods on both single and multi-step generation datasets with traceable hallucination detection.

papers.title: What Makes Effective Supervision in Latent Chain-of-Thought: An Information-Theoretic Analysis
papers.contribution: Shows reasoning accuracy depends on information fidelity in latent chains; demonstrates generative reconstruction better preserves semantic structure than rigid geometric compression.

papers.title: “very likely” Means “uncertain”? How LLMs Diverge from Humans in Linguistic Uncertainty Quantification
papers.contribution: VOCAL reveals systematic confidence disparities between humans and LLMs in verbal expressions, enabling marker-level comparison of confidence semantics and disentangling semantic mismatch.
